headline: Hollywood is making films about Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk and Sam Altman as public worry about AI grows.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: the three films are confirmed by a second outlet (CNET), though CNBC’s own page could not be opened and the effect on opinion is only a comparison.
importance_line: Hollywood's turn on the leaders of the AI era may shape how viewers see the industry first, then the three executives and their companies, but that effect is only suggested by a comparison with earlier films, not shown.
summary: CNBC reports, in an account relayed by The News International, that films about Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Tesla’s Elon Musk and OpenAI’s Sam Altman are reaching audiences as public worry about AI and its data centers grows: Aaron Sorkin’s “The Social Reckoning”, Alex Gibney’s nearly four-hour documentary “Musk” and, at Christmas, the Altman film “Artificial”. Altman told CNBC “I get why people have anxiety” and that being teased does not bother him, while Musk has attacked the documentary on X, saying it lacks integrity.
notes: CNBC page returned 403. Text read from The News International (rewrite of the CNBC story, page https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1419417-hollywood-takes-aim-at-zuckerberg-musk-and-altman-over-ai-fears) and cross-checked in CNET (https://www.cnet.com/culture/entertainment/hollywood-movies-ai-tech-zuckerberg-musk/, 9 Oct 2026). Link kept on CNBC as the original. Release dates left out because the two outlets differ.
